verdict.reason: All claimed evidence checks out. `text-box-editor.ts:841` carries the literal comment "Mirrors `getSelectionStyleImpl` in `view/editor.ts`", and `caretStyle` (847-863) is a near-verbatim duplicate of `editor.ts:1001-1017` (same findBlock lookup, same resolveStyleInline defaults layer, same `offset <= inlineEnd` scan, same trailing-inline fallback). `text-editor.ts:2966-2980` + `styleDefaultsAtCursor` (2988-2992) is a third copy of the same caret walk, and the copies already differ (getBlock vs findBlock), confirming the drift risk. The reuse target genuinely exists in the right layer: `model/range-runs.ts:49-81` already performs the identical per-block defaults+inline.style layering and was adopted for the range branch (text-box-editor.ts:906, text-editor.ts:3017) while the caret branch stayed hand-copied. The change's own lessons doc rejects exactly this pattern at docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-lessons.md:42 and :54. Duplication/reuse is explicitly in the design-fit lane and rated major by the rubric; the code is reachable (used by getSelectionStyle at :996 and getRangeStyleSummary at :1013). No not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies.

finding.summary: The stated "read = write by construction" invariant is not actually structural for cell-rectangle selections: the read dispatches on `range.tableCellRange`, the model write silently ignores it
finding.evidence: `visitStyledRunsInRange` (model/range-runs.ts:76-80) routes a `DocRange` carrying `tableCellRange` to `visitCellRectangleSlices`, while `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (model/document.ts:360) passes the same `DocRange` to `visitRangeSlices`, which deliberately ignores `tableCellRange` (range-slices.ts:93-95). Agreement therefore still depends on every caller pre-routing rectangles to `applyInlineStyleToCells` in the view layer (editor.ts:1043, text-editor.ts:2924) — a maintained convention, not a structural guarantee. A model-level caller (e.g. a future pending-style or collaboration path) that hands a rectangle range to `applyInlineStyle` reintroduces exactly the #715 read/write disagreement the design section claims is now impossible (docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md, "The shared range traversal").

verdict.reason: The code is present as described (range-runs.ts:76-80 dispatches on tableCellRange; document.ts:360-365 does not; range-slices.ts:93-95 deliberately ignores it; view-layer routing at editor.ts:1043-1049 and text-editor.ts:2924-2929), but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (1) The originating task's rectangle acceptance criterion explicitly prescribes editor-layer routing — "Route both editors' applyStyleToCellRange through Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells / visitCellRectangleSlices ... Clamp the rectangle to the table's dimensions" (todo:75-78) — and that is exactly what shipped (document.ts:373-381, range-slices.ts:43-67 with clamping at 51-59). The "read = write by construction" item (todo:67-70) is scoped to collapsing the read walk and Doc.applyInlineStyle into visitRangeSlices, which is done. (2) The design doc does not overclaim: docs-font-controls.md:316-322 states the structural guarantee for visitRangeSlices and then explicitly carves the rectangle out as "a selection shape of its own" with a sibling traversal driven by the read and by Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells; the same carve-out is documented at document.ts:357-358 and range-slices.ts:93-95. The doc is canonical and in-place, not parallel or missing. (3) No duplication (one shared rectangle walk serves read and write) and no Non-Goal exceeded. What is left is a request that the model-level applyInlineStyle also dispatch on tableCellRange for future-proofing — an API-symmetry/robustness preference, which this rubric classifies as minor/nit and never blocking. A concrete caller that mis-routes a rectangle today would be a line-level routing bug for the correctness lens, not this lens, and is not what the finding alleges.

finding.summary: The new shared walk re-implements `Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s dispatch rather than becoming its single source of truth — the read/write drift the fix targets is only halved
finding.evidence: `visitStyledRunsInRange` (range-runs.ts:96-183) hand-copies all four branches of `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:349-440): same-block, cross-block-in-cell, top-level with `blockParentMap` normalization, table-read-whole. The module's own header says "Mirrors `Doc.applyInlineStyle` so the runs read are the runs written" — i.e. correctness now depends on two independent copies of the same dispatch staying identical, which is exactly the failure mode issue #715 describes. The obvious fit here is one traversal in `model/` that both the read (summary/step/keyboard) and the write (`applyInlineStyle`, via a `visit` that calls `store.applyStyle`) drive; the walk touches only `Doc`/model state (findBlock, blockParentMap, getContextBlocks, resolveStyleInline) and has no layout dependency, so placing it under `view/` is also a layer mismatch for a model-level traversal.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. (1) There is no packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts; the file is packages/docs/src/model/range-runs.ts, already in the model layer, so the alleged layer mismatch is absent. (2) The file is 82 lines, so the cited range-runs.ts:96-183 body does not exist; those line numbers actually correspond to visitRangeSlices in model/range-slices.ts:102-183. (3) The quoted header "Mirrors Doc.applyInlineStyle so the runs read are the runs written" is not in the file; the actual header (range-runs.ts:1-18) states the module delegates the which-text question to visitRangeSlices, "the same traversal Doc.applyInlineStyle writes through". (4) No duplication of the four dispatch branches exists: visitStyledRunsInRange only builds a per-slice closure and delegates to visitCellRectangleSlices/visitRangeSlices (range-runs.ts:76-81), while Doc.applyInlineStyle (document.ts:360-365) and applyInlineStyleToCells (document.ts:373-381) drive the same two functions with a visitor that calls store.applyStyle. The four branches (same block, cross-block-in-cell, top-level with blockParentMap normalization, table-whole) appear exactly once, in model/range-slices.ts:102-183. The repo already implements the very single-source-of-truth design the finding prescribes as the fix.

finding.summary: The diff cements "a nested table's content is never styled by a range toggle" as intended design, contradicting docs-nested-tables.md's stated Goal of full styling parity inside nested tables, without updating that doc
finding.evidence: The new doc section states nested content "is never written — and reading what cannot be written re-creates the #715 trap", and packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts pins it (`expect(storedInner.inlines[0].style.bold).toBeUndefined()` — "Untouched: the write never descends into the nested table"). docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:21-22 lists as a Goal: "Full feature parity inside nested tables: cell merge/split, row/column insert/delete, resize, styling", and its Non-Goals (lines 28-32) do not exempt styling. Either `applyInlineStyle` should recurse (fixing the write) or the nested-tables doc must record the exception; codifying the gap in a different doc plus a regression test leaves the two design docs in conflict.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that docs-nested-tables.md was left unmodified and therefore in conflict with the new docs-font-controls.md section. That is not the state of the repository. The Goal line the reviewer quotes (docs-nested-tables.md:21-23) actually reads "...resize, styling (one exception ships today — see [Known gap](#known-gap-inline-styling-does-not-descend))" — the qualifier the finding says is missing is on the quoted line itself. The doc additionally contains a dedicated "### Known gap: inline styling does not descend" section at lines 35-61 describing precisely this behavior (visitRangeSlices not recursing into nested table blocks, the endpoint no-op, what closing it would require, and why read and write are kept symmetric per #715). docs-font-controls.md:339 links to that exact anchor, so the gap is recorded once in the canonical subsystem doc with a pointer from the other — not a parallel/duplicate doc. The test at backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:635-637 exists as quoted but pins behavior that the nested-tables doc now explicitly documents, so no doc/test conflict remains. The reconciliation was an intentional tracked item (20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:84-86). Ground: not-present.
